english: "Ah, well done!" — this cry, smooth and deep, raised in the sky by beings out of joy, resounded through the three worlds.
notes: bhūtaiḥ: 'beings' (could also mean spirits or elemental beings). anvavādayat: literally 'caused to sound along/after', i.e. made the worlds echo.

hindi: शुभ वायु बहने लगी, सभी दिशाएँ प्रकाश से खिल उठीं, और जल से युक्त दिव्य पुष्प-वर्षाएँ भी हुईं।
english: An auspicious wind blew, all the directions shone open with radiance, and heavenly showers of flowers, together with water, fell.
notes: sajalāḥ: 'with water', i.e. the flower showers came with drops of water (or with rain).

hindi: तब ज्ञान की देवियाँ — बुद्धि, सिद्धि, स्मृति, मेधा, धृति, कीर्ति, क्षमा और दया — अग्निवेश आदि में प्रविष्ट हुईं।
english: Then the deities of knowledge — Intellect (buddhi), Accomplishment (siddhi), Memory (smṛti), Retention (medhā), Steadfastness (dhṛti), Fame (kīrti), Forbearance (kṣamā) and Compassion (dayā) — entered Agniveśa and the others headed by him.
notes: kṣamādayā is printed as one token; it is two nominatives kṣamā and dayā written together (no sandhi change). A reading kṣamā-ādayaḥ 'forbearance and the rest' would need a different text.
lines_deva: बुद्धिः सिद्धिः स्मृतिर्मेधा धृतिः कीर्तिः क्षमादया
lines_iast: buddhiḥ siddhiḥ smṛtirmedhā dhṛtiḥ kīrtiḥ kṣamādayā

hindi: और इनके वे तन्त्र-ग्रन्थ परम ऋषियों द्वारा अनुमोदित होकर प्राणि-समूहों के कल्याण के लिए पृथ्वी पर प्रतिष्ठित हुए।
english: And those treatises (tantra) of theirs, approved by the supreme sages, gained an established place on earth for the welfare of the multitudes of beings.
notes: eṣām 'of these' refers to Agniveśa and his fellow pupils of the preceding verses. bhava: 'welfare, well-being' (also 'existence').

hindi: जिसमें हितकर और अहितकर, सुखी और दुःखी आयु, उस आयु के लिए हित और अहित, उसका मान तथा स्वयं वह आयु बताई गई है, वह आयुर्वेद कहलाता है।
english: That in which wholesome and unwholesome life, happy and unhappy life, what is wholesome and unwholesome for it, its measure, and life itself are described, is called Āyurveda (the science of life).

text_flags.why: the word for 'unhappy/sorrow' is duḥkha; the visarga is missing; likely typo (sense requires duḥkha, the opposite of sukha)

notes: Usual reading: four kinds of life (hita, ahita, sukha, duḥkha āyus); tasya hitāhitam = what is good and bad for life; mānam = its measure (length); tat = life itself.
lines_deva: मानं च तच्च यत्रोक्तमायुर्वेदः स उच्यते
lines_iast: mānaṃ ca tacca yatroktamāyurvedaḥ sa ucyate

words.gloss: union of body, senses, mind and self
words.gram: m. nom. sg. tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: शरीर, इन्द्रिय, सत्त्व अर्थात् मन और आत्मा का संयोग आयु है; धारि, जीवित, नित्यग और अनुबन्ध — इन पर्यायों से आयु कही जाती है।
english: The union of body, senses, mind (sattva) and self (ātman) is life (āyus); it is called by the synonyms dhāri (sustaining), jīvita (living), nityaga (ever-moving) and anubandha (continuity).
notes: āyuḥ in 42b is the predicate of the whole verse: the union is āyus, and dhāri, jīvita, nityaga, anubandha are its synonyms.

words.gloss: of the knowers of the Vedas

hindi: आयु का वह वेद, जिसे वेदज्ञ सबसे पुण्यमय मानते हैं और जो मनुष्यों के लिए दोनों लोकों में हितकर है, आगे कहा जाएगा।
english: The science (veda) of that life, regarded by the knowers of the Vedas as the most sacred, which is beneficial to humans in both worlds, will be taught.
notes: yat (n.) refers to vedaḥ (m.) by sense, or means 'what is beneficial'. lokayor ubhayoḥ: 'this world and the next'; the dual could also be genitive. vakṣyate is a middle future used passively.

hindi: सब पदार्थों की वृद्धि का कारण सदा सामान्य है और ह्रास का कारण विशेष है; प्रवृत्ति तो दोनों की होती है।
english: Sameness (sāmānya) is always the cause of increase of all entities, and difference (viśeṣa) the cause of decrease; but application belongs to both.
notes: pravṛttir ubhayasya tu is read in different ways: both are applied (in treatment), or both operate together on things. Kept literal.

hindi: सामान्य एकत्व करने वाला है और विशेष पृथक्त्व करने वाला; तुल्यार्थता ही सामान्य है और विशेष उसका विपरीत है।
english: Sameness (sāmānya) produces oneness, while difference (viśeṣa) produces separateness; sameness is indeed likeness of things, and difference is the opposite.

hindi: सत्त्व अर्थात् मन, आत्मा और शरीर — यह त्रय त्रिदण्ड के समान है; इनके संयोग से लोक टिका रहता है, और उसी में सब प्रतिष्ठित है।
english: Mind (sattva), self and body — this triad is like a tripod; by their union the world (of living beings) stands, and in it everything is established.
notes: tridaṇḍa: three staffs tied together that stand only jointly. loka is taken by commentators as the living person; tatra may refer to that union.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. ppp. caus. sam-pra-√kāś

hindi: वही पुरुष है, वही चेतन है, और वही इस वेद का अधिकरण अर्थात् विषय माना गया है; उसी के लिए यह वेद प्रकाशित किया गया है।
english: That (union) is the person (pumān); it is sentient; and it is declared the subject matter of this science; for its sake this science has been revealed.
notes: saḥ (m.) agrees with pumān; the following tat (n.) refers to the union (saṃyoga) of the previous verse.

hindi: आकाश आदि, आत्मा, मन, काल और दिशाएँ — यह द्रव्यों का संग्रह है; इन्द्रियों से युक्त द्रव्य चेतन है और इन्द्रियरहित द्रव्य अचेतन।
english: Ether and the others, the self, mind, time and the directions — this is the group of substances (dravya). A substance with senses is sentient; one without senses is insentient.
notes: khādīni: the five elements beginning with kha (ether).

hindi: अर्थों सहित गुरु आदि, बुद्धि, तथा प्रयत्न तक के पर आदि — ये गुण कहे गए हैं; प्रयत्न-पूर्वक होने वाली चेष्टा कर्म कहलाती है।
english: The qualities (guṇa) are declared to be: the sense objects (artha), together with heaviness and the rest (guru etc.), intellect (buddhi), and para and the rest ending with effort (prayatna). Movement preceded by effort is called action (karma).
notes: sārthāḥ: with the arthas (sound, touch, form, taste, smell). parādayaḥ prayatnāntāḥ: the list para, apara, yukti, saṃkhyā, saṃyoga, vibhāga, pṛthaktva, parimāṇa, saṃskāra, abhyāsa, given later in the text (Sūtrasthāna 26), ending with prayatna. prayatnādi karma may also be read 'action begins with effort'.

hindi: पृथ्वी आदि का गुणों के साथ अपृथग्भाव समवाय माना गया है; वह नित्य है, क्योंकि जहाँ द्रव्य है वहाँ गुण अनियत नहीं होता।
english: Inherence (samavāya) is held to be the inseparable existence of earth and the other substances with their qualities; it is eternal, for where there is a substance, quality is not unfixed there.
lines_deva: स नित्यो यत्र हि द्रव्यं न तत्रानियतो गुणः
lines_iast: sa nityo yatra hi dravyaṃ na tatrāniyato guṇaḥ

hindi: जिसमें कर्म और गुण आश्रित रहते हैं और जो समवायी कारण है, वह द्रव्य है; गुण तो समवायी, निश्चेष्ट कारण है।
english: That in which actions and qualities reside and which is the inherent (samavāyin) cause is substance (dravya); quality (guṇa), however, is an inherent but motionless cause.
lines_deva: तद्द्रव्यं समवायी तु निश्चेष्टः कारणं गुणः
lines_iast: taddravyaṃ samavāyī tu niśceṣṭaḥ kāraṇaṃ guṇaḥ

words.gloss: of what is to be done

hindi: जो द्रव्य में आश्रित रहकर संयोग और विभाग का कारण है और करने योग्य की क्रिया है, वह कर्म है; कर्म किसी अन्य की अपेक्षा नहीं करता।
english: That which, residing in a substance, is the cause of conjunction and disjunction, and is the activity of what is to be done, is action (karma); action depends on nothing else.
notes: Usual reading: karma needs nothing else to cause conjunction and disjunction. dravyam āśritam: 'resting on a substance' (dravyam as object of āśrita).
lines_deva: संयोगे च विभागे च कारणं द्रव्यमाश्रितम्
lines_iast: saṃyoge ca vibhāge ca kāraṇaṃ dravyamāśritam

words.gloss: effect, what is to be achieved
bringing about equilibrium of the dhātus

hindi: इस प्रकार कारण कहा गया। यहाँ धातुओं की समता को कार्य कहा जाता है, और धातु-साम्य की क्रिया इस तन्त्र का प्रयोजन कही गई है।
english: Thus the cause has been stated. Here the effect (kārya) is said to be the equilibrium of the dhātus, and the act of bringing about that equilibrium is declared the purpose of this treatise.

words.gloss: of time, intellect and sense objects

hindi: काल, बुद्धि और इन्द्रियार्थों का मिथ्या योग, अयोग और अतियोग — यह दो आश्रयों वाले रोगों के कारणों का तीन प्रकार का संग्रह है।
english: Wrong, deficient (non-) and excessive conjunction of time, intellect and sense objects — this is the threefold summary of the causes of diseases, which have two seats.
notes: yogo mithyā na cāti ca = mithyāyoga, ayoga, atiyoga. indriyārtha read as 'sense objects' (it could also be split indriya + artha, senses and their objects). The two seats are body and mind (next verse).
lines_deva: कालबुद्धीन्द्रियार्थानां योगो मिथ्या न चाति च
lines_iast: kālabuddhīndriyārthānāṃ yogo mithyā na cāti ca

hindi: शरीर और सत्त्व नामक मन रोगों के आश्रय माने गए हैं, और वैसे ही सुखों के भी; सुखों का कारण तो सम योग है।
english: The body and that which is called sattva (the mind) are held to be the seat of diseases, and likewise of well-being (sukha); the cause of well-being is balanced conjunction.
notes: sukha here is commonly taken as health (the opposite of vyādhi). samaḥ yogaḥ = samayoga, proper conjunction of time, intellect and sense objects.
lines_deva: तथा सुखानां योगस्तु सुखानां कारणं समः
lines_iast: tathā sukhānāṃ yogastu sukhānāṃ kāraṇaṃ samaḥ

words.gloss: with mind, qualities of the elements and senses

hindi: आत्मा तो निर्विकार और पर है; वह सत्त्व, भूतों के गुणों और इन्द्रियों के साथ मिलकर चैतन्य का कारण है; वह नित्य और द्रष्टा है, क्योंकि वह क्रियाओं को देखता है।
english: The self, however, is changeless and supreme; together with the mind, the qualities of the elements and the senses, it is the cause of consciousness; it is eternal and the seer, for it sees actions.
notes: sattvabhūtaguṇendriyaiḥ: bhūtaguṇa may be 'qualities of the elements' or 'elements and qualities' taken separately. The instrumental is taken as 'together with'.
lines_deva: चैतन्ये कारणं नित्यो द्रष्टा पश्यति हि क्रियाः
lines_iast: caitanye kāraṇaṃ nityo draṣṭā paśyati hi kriyāḥ

hindi: वायु, पित्त और कफ — यह शारीरिक दोषों का संग्रह कहा गया है; और मानस दोष रज और तम बताए गए हैं।
english: Vāyu (Vāta), Pitta and Kapha are stated to be the group of bodily doṣas; the mental group, on the other hand, is indicated as Rajas and Tamas.
lines_deva: मानसः पुनरुद्दिष्टो रजश्च तम एव च
lines_iast: mānasaḥ punaruddiṣṭo rajaśca tama eva ca

words.gloss: based on the divine and on reasoning
by knowledge, understanding, fortitude, memory and concentration

hindi: पहला अर्थात् शारीरिक दोष-समूह दैवव्यपाश्रय और युक्तिव्यपाश्रय औषधों से शान्त होता है; मानस दोष ज्ञान, विज्ञान, धैर्य, स्मृति और समाधि से।
english: The former (the bodily group) is pacified by remedies based on the divine (daiva-vyapāśraya) and on reasoning (yukti-vyapāśraya); the mental group by knowledge, understanding, fortitude, memory and concentration (samādhi).

hindi: वात रूक्ष, शीत, लघु, सूक्ष्म, चल, विशद और खर है; वह विपरीत गुणों वाले द्रव्यों से शान्त होता है।
english: Vāta (māruta, wind) is dry, cold, light, subtle, mobile, non-slimy (viśada) and rough; it is pacified by substances with opposite qualities.
notes: The adjectives of 59a agree with mārutaḥ in 59b.
lines_deva: रूक्षः शीतो लघुः सूक्ष्मश्चलोऽथ विशदः खरः
lines_iast: rūkṣaḥ śīto laghuḥ sūkṣmaścalo'tha viśadaḥ kharaḥ

hindi: पित्त स्नेह से युक्त, उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, द्रव, अम्ल, सर और कटु है; वह विपरीत गुणों वाले द्रव्यों से शीघ्र शान्त होता है।
english: Pitta is unctuous (sasneha), hot, sharp, liquid, sour, flowing (sara) and pungent; it is quickly pacified by substances with opposite qualities.
notes: sasneha: literally 'with unctuousness'; commentators take it as 'slightly unctuous'.
lines_deva: सस्नेहमुष्णं तीक्ष्णं च द्रवमम्लं सरं कटु
lines_iast: sasnehamuṣṇaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ ca dravamamlaṃ saraṃ kaṭu

words.gloss: heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, sweet, stable, slimy

hindi: कफ के गुरु, शीत, मृदु, स्निग्ध, मधुर, स्थिर और पिच्छिल गुण विपरीत गुणों से शान्त होते हैं।
english: The qualities of Kapha (śleṣman) — heavy, cold, soft, unctuous, sweet, stable and slimy — are pacified by opposite qualities.

words.gloss: administered with regard to place, dose and time

hindi: विपरीत गुणों वाली और देश, मात्रा तथा काल के अनुसार प्रयुक्त औषधियों से साध्य माने गए विकार दूर हो जाते हैं।
english: Disorders regarded as curable are reversed by medicines of opposite qualities, administered with due regard to place, dose and time.

hindi: परन्तु असाध्य रोगों की चिकित्सा का उपदेश नहीं किया जाता। इसके आगे प्रत्येक द्रव्य के अनुसार गुण और कर्म बताए जाएँगे।
english: But treatment of incurable diseases is not taught. Further, from here on, the qualities and actions will be stated substance by substance.
notes: guṇakarmāṇi is the acc. pl. object of vakṣyate (3 sg. fut. middle, the teacher as the implied subject: '(he) will state the qualities and actions'); there is no agreement problem. The English passive is idiomatic.

hindi: रसना इन्द्रिय का विषय रस है; उसका द्रव्य जल और पृथ्वी हैं; उसकी उत्पत्ति और विशेषता में आकाश आदि तीन कारण हैं।
english: Taste (rasa) is the object of the tongue; its substratum is water and also earth; in its formation and its differentiation the three beginning with ether are the causes.
notes: The three beginning with kha are ether, air and fire. Commentators differ on whether nirvṛtti also involves water and earth.
lines_deva: निर्वृत्तौ च विशेषे च प्रत्ययाः खादयस्त्रयः
lines_iast: nirvṛttau ca viśeṣe ca pratyayāḥ khādayastrayaḥ

hindi: मधुर, अम्ल, लवण, कटु, तिक्त और कषाय — रसों का यह छह का संग्रह कहा गया है।
english: Sweet, sour, salty, pungent, bitter and astringent — this set of six is held to be the summary of the tastes (rasa).

hindi: मधुर, अम्ल और लवण रस वायु को; कषाय, मधुर और तिक्त रस पित्त को; तथा कषाय, कटु और तिक्त रस कफ को जीतते हैं।
english: Sweet, sour and salty tastes overcome Vāyu (Vāta); astringent, sweet and bitter overcome Pitta; astringent, pungent and bitter overcome Kapha.

hindi: कुछ द्रव्य दोषों को शान्त करने वाले हैं, कुछ धातुओं को दूषित करने वाले, और कुछ स्वस्थवृत्त में उपयोगी माने गए हैं — इस प्रकार द्रव्य तीन प्रकार का कहा जाता है।
english: Some substances pacify the doṣas, some vitiate the dhātus, and some are approved for maintaining health — thus substance (dravya) is said to be threefold.

hindi: वह द्रव्य फिर तीन प्रकार का कहा गया है — जांगम, औद्भिद और पार्थिव। मधु, गोरस, पित्त, वसा, मज्जा, रक्त, मांस,
english: That (substance) again is declared threefold: animal (jaṅgama), plant-born (audbhida) and earthly (pārthiva). Honeys, cow products, bile, fat, marrow, blood, flesh,
notes: The list of animal products in 68b continues into 69, which ends 'are used from animals'; the edition's grouping is kept. madhūni: plural, the kinds of honey. pitta here is animal bile, not the doṣa.

words.gloss: faeces, urine, skin, semen, bone, sinew, horn, nails

hindi: मल, मूत्र, चर्म, वीर्य, अस्थि, स्नायु, सींग, नख, खुर, केश, रोम और रोचना — ये जांगम द्रव्यों से लेकर प्रयोग में लाए जाते हैं।
english: faeces, urine, skin, semen, bone, sinew, horn, nails, hooves, head hair, body hair and rocanā are the things used from animals.
notes: Continues the list begun in 68b. retosthi = retas + asthi inside the compound (printed without avagraha). rocanā: standard identification gorocanā, a gallstone (bezoar) of cattle.

hindi: सोना, मल सहित पाँच लोह, बालू, सुधा अर्थात् चूना, मैनसिल और हरताल, मणियाँ, लवण, गेरू और अञ्जन —
english: Gold, the five metals (loha) with their dross (mala), along with sand, lime (sudhā), realgar (manaḥśilā) and orpiment (āla), gems, salt, red ochre (gairika) and añjana (collyrium mineral) —
notes: The sentence ends in 71a ('are indicated as earthly medicine'). sasikatāḥ may qualify lohāḥ ('together with sand') or simply add sand (sikatā) to the list. The five metals are not named here; commentators usually give copper, silver, tin, lead and iron (disputed). manaḥśilā = realgar (standard); āla = haritāla, orpiment (standard); gairika = red ochre (standard); añjana = stibnite/antimony sulphide (probable; galena also proposed, disputed).
lines_deva: सुवर्णं समलाः पञ्च लोहाः ससिकताः सुधा
lines_iast: suvarṇaṃ samalāḥ pañca lohāḥ sasikatāḥ sudhā

hindi: ये पार्थिव औषध बताए गए हैं। औद्भिद औषध तो चार प्रकार का है — वनस्पति, वीरुध्, वानस्पत्य और ओषधि।
english: — are indicated as earthly medicine. The plant-born, however, is fourfold: vanaspati, vīrudh, vānaspatya and oṣadhi.
notes: 71a completes the list of 70. The four plant classes are defined in 72.

words.gloss: ending with the ripening of fruit

hindi: वनस्पति फलों से, वानस्पत्य फूलों और फलों से पहचाने जाते हैं; ओषधियाँ वे हैं जिनका अन्त फल पकने पर होता है, और वीरुध् फैलने वाली बेलों से पहचाने गए हैं।
english: Vanaspati is known by its fruits, vānaspatya by flowers and also fruits; oṣadhis are those whose life ends with the ripening of their fruit; and vīrudhs are known by their spreading runners.
notes: Commentators take vanaspati as a tree bearing fruit without evident flowers (e.g. figs) and vānaspatya as one with both flowers and fruit. The text itself only says 'by fruits', 'by flowers and fruits'.

hindi: जड़, छाल, सार, निर्यास, नाल, स्वरस, कोमल पत्ते, क्षार, क्षीर, फल, फूल, भस्म, तेल, काँटे,
english: Root, bark, heartwood, exudate, stalk, expressed juice, tender leaves, alkalis, milky latex, fruit, flower, ash, oils, thorns,
notes: The list of plant parts used as drugs continues into 74a, where it is summed up as the plant (audbhida) group. kṣīra here is the milky sap of plants, not animal milk (context of plant products).
lines_deva: क्षाराः क्षीरं फलं पुष्पं भस्म तैलानि कण्टकाः
lines_iast: kṣārāḥ kṣīraṃ phalaṃ puṣpaṃ bhasma tailāni kaṇṭakāḥ

hindi: पत्ते, कोंपलें, कन्द और अंकुर — यह औद्भिद गण है। मूलिनी सोलह और फलिनी उन्नीस कही गई हैं।
english: leaves, leaf-buds, bulbs and shoots: this is the plant (audbhida) group. The root-drugs (mūlinī) are declared to be sixteen and the fruit-drugs (phalinī) nineteen.
notes: ekonā goes with viṃśatiḥ: "twenty less one" = nineteen (confirmed by 86a phalāny ekonaviṃśatiḥ). mūlinī = plants whose root is the useful part; phalinī = plants whose fruit is used.

hindi: चार महास्नेह और पाँच ही लवण हैं; आठ मूत्र गिनाए गए हैं और आठ ही दूध।
english: There are four great fats (mahāsneha) and just five salts; eight urines are enumerated, and likewise eight milks.

words.gram: ppp. m. nom. pl. ni-√dṛś caus.

hindi: और शोधन के लिए छह वृक्ष पुनर्वसु ने बताए हैं। जो इन्हें रोगों में प्रयोग करना जानता है, वह वेद का ज्ञाता है।
english: And six trees for purification (śodhana) have been pointed out by Punarvasu. He who knows how to apply these in disorders is a knower of the Veda.
notes: Punarvasu: name of the teacher (Punarvasu Ātreya in this text). vedavit: literally "knower of the Veda"; it may mean the knower of this science (Āyurveda) rather than of the Vedas generally. The six trees are not named in this chunk.
lines_deva: य एतान् वेत्ति संयोक्तुं विकारेषु स वेदवित्
lines_iast: ya etān vetti saṃyoktuṃ vikāreṣu sa vedavit

hindi: हस्तिदन्ती, हैमवती, श्यामा, त्रिवृत्, अधोगुडा, सप्तला, श्वेता नाम वाली, प्रत्यक्श्रेणी और गवाक्षी भी,
english: Hastidantī, haimavatī, śyāmā, trivṛt, adhoguḍā, saptalā, the one named śvetā, pratyakśreṇī and also gavākṣī,
notes: List of the sixteen root-drugs (mūlinī), continued in 78. Identifications: trivṛt = Operculina turpethum, Hindi निशोथ (standard); śyāmā = the dark variety of trivṛt (probable); hastidantī = a large dantī, Baliospermum montanum or allied (disputed); pratyakśreṇī = dantī, Baliospermum montanum, Hindi दन्ती (probable); haimavatī = disputed (white vacā or Iris species proposed); adhoguḍā = disputed (Argyreia nervosa, vṛddhadāruka, proposed); saptalā = disputed (an Acacia or Euphorbia species proposed); śvetā = disputed (white-flowered Clitoria ternatea, Hindi अपराजिता, often proposed); gavākṣī = disputed (a colocynth-like cucurbit, indravāruṇī type, proposed).

hindi: ज्योतिष्मती, बिम्बी, शणपुष्पी, विषाणिका, अजगन्धा, द्रवन्ती और यहाँ सोलहवीं क्षीरिणी है।
english: jyotiṣmatī, bimbī, śaṇapuṣpī, viṣāṇikā, ajagandhā, dravantī, and kṣīriṇī, the sixteenth here.
notes: Identifications: jyotiṣmatī = Celastrus paniculatus, Hindi मालकांगनी (standard); bimbī = Coccinia grandis, Hindi कुंदरू (standard); śaṇapuṣpī = Crotalaria verrucosa or allied, Hindi झुनझुनिया (probable); ajagandhā = Cleome gynandra or Gynandropsis, Hindi हुरहुर (probable); viṣāṇikā = disputed (Helicteres isora and others proposed); dravantī = disputed (a Croton or Jatropha species proposed); kṣīriṇī = disputed (a latex-bearing plant; several candidates). Count 77+78 = 16, matching 74b.
lines_deva: ज्योतिष्मती च बिम्बी च शणपुष्पी विषाणिका
अजगन्धा द्रवन्ती च क्षीरिणी चात्र षोडशी
lines_iast: jyotiṣmatī ca bimbī ca śaṇapuṣpī viṣāṇikā
ajagandhā dravantī ca kṣīriṇī cātra ṣoḍaśī

hindi: शणपुष्पी, बिम्बी और हैमवती भी वमन में, तथा श्वेता और ज्योतिष्मती शिरोविरेचन में प्रयोग करनी चाहिए।
english: Śaṇapuṣpī, bimbī and also haimavatī are to be used in emesis (vamana), and śvetā and jyotiṣmatī in head-evacuation (śīrṣavirecana, errhine therapy).
notes: "ca cchardane": the doubled cch is regular sandhi after a short vowel (ca + chardane); not a typo. yojyā is singular but applies to each plant named.
lines_deva: शणपुष्पी च बिम्बी च च्छर्दने हैमवत्यपि
lines_iast: śaṇapuṣpī ca bimbī ca cchardane haimavatyapi

hindi: जो ग्यारह शेष रहीं, उन्हें विरेचन में प्रयोग करना चाहिए। इस प्रकार नाम और कर्म से मूलिनी बता दी गईं; अब फलिनी सुनो।
english: The eleven that remain are to be used in purgation (virecana). Thus the root-drugs have been described by name and action; now hear the fruit-drugs.
notes: 16 root-drugs minus the 5 assigned in 79 (śaṇapuṣpī, bimbī, haimavatī for emesis; śvetā, jyotiṣmatī for head-evacuation) = 11.

hindi: शङ्खिनी, फिर विडङ्ग, त्रपुष और मदन; धामार्गव, फिर इक्ष्वाकु, जीमूत और कृतवेधन; तथा क्लीतक, जो आनूप और स्थलज भेद से दो प्रकार का कहा गया है,
english: Śaṅkhinī, then viḍaṅga, trapuṣa and madana; dhāmārgava, then ikṣvāku, jīmūta and kṛtavedhana; and klītaka, declared to be of two kinds, marsh-grown and land-grown,

text_flags.why: dvididha is not a word; dvi-vidha "of two kinds" fits sense and matches caturvidhaḥ in 86b.

notes: Line b recurs as 83b; this is not a duplication error: here it is part of the list of the 19 fruit-drugs, and at 83b it begins the list of their uses (83b + 84a = eight emetics). trapuṣam: the usual spelling is trapusa (dental s); trapuṣa is a known variant, so not flagged as an error. Identifications: viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes, Hindi वायविडंग (standard); trapusa = Cucumis sativus, cucumber, Hindi खीरा (standard); madana = Catunaregam spinosa (Randia dumetorum), Hindi मैनफल (standard); ikṣvāku = bitter Lagenaria siceraria, Hindi कड़वी तुम्बी (standard); dhāmārgava = a Luffa species, Hindi तोरई type (probable); jīmūta = Luffa echinata, Hindi देवदाली (probable); kṛtavedhana = bitter Luffa acutangula, कोशातकी (probable); klītaka = liquorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra, Hindi मुलेठी (probable; it is a root, which commentators discuss); śaṅkhinī = disputed.
lines_deva: आनूपं स्थलजं चैव क्लीतकं द्विदिधं स्मृतम्
lines_iast: ānūpaṃ sthalajaṃ caiva klītakaṃ dvididhaṃ smṛtam

hindi: प्रकीर्या, उदकीर्या, प्रत्यक्पुष्पा तथा अभया, अन्तःकोटरपुष्पी और हस्तिपर्णी का शरद् ऋतु का फल,
english: prakīryā and udakīryā, pratyakpuṣpā and likewise abhayā, antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī, and the autumn-gathered fruit of hastiparṇī,
notes: śāradam ("autumnal") is taken with an understood phalam: the fruit of hastiparṇī gathered in autumn. Identifications: pratyakpuṣpā = Achyranthes aspera, Hindi अपामार्ग, चिरचिटा (standard); abhayā = Terminalia chebula, Hindi हरड़ (standard); prakīryā = Caesalpinia bonduc or a karañja, Hindi पूतिकरंज (probable); udakīryā = Pongamia pinnata, Hindi करंज (probable); antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī = disputed (nīlinī and others proposed); hastiparṇī = disputed.

hindi: कम्पिल्लक और आरग्वध का फल, और कुटज का भी। धामार्गव, फिर इक्ष्वाकु, जीमूत, कृतवेधन,
english: the fruit of kampillaka and of āragvadha, and that of kuṭaja. Dhāmārgava, then ikṣvāku, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana,
notes: GROUPING: line a ends the list of fruit-drugs; line b repeats 81b but starts a new sentence (the drugs for emesis and āsthāpana) that runs into 84a. The sense-grouping would be 83a with the list, and 83b + 84 together. Count of the fruit list (81a, 81b, 81c, 82, 83a): śaṅkhinī, viḍaṅga, trapuṣa, madana, dhāmārgava, ikṣvāku, jīmūta, kṛtavedhana, klītaka of two kinds (2), prakīryā, udakīryā, pratyakpuṣpā, abhayā, antaḥkoṭarapuṣpī, hastiparṇī, kampillaka, āragvadha, kuṭaja = 19. Identifications: kampillaka = Mallotus philippensis, Hindi कमीला (standard); āragvadha = Cassia fistula, Hindi अमलतास (standard); kuṭaja = Holarrhena pubescens (H. antidysenterica), Hindi कुड़ा (standard).

hindi: मदन, कुटज, त्रपुष और हस्तिपर्णिनी — इन सबको वमन में और आस्थापन बस्तियों में प्रयोग करना चाहिए।
english: madana, kuṭaja, trapuṣa and hastiparṇinī: these are to be used in emesis (vamana) and in decoction enemas (āsthāpana).
notes: etāni covers the eight drugs of 83b and 84a. hastiparṇinī is taken as the same plant as hastiparṇī of 82b.

hindi: प्रत्यक्पुष्पा नाक के मार्ग से प्रच्छर्दन में विहित है। जो दस शेष हैं, वे विरेचन में बताए गए हैं।
english: Pratyakpuṣpā is prescribed for evacuation through the nose. The ten that remain are stated for purgation (virecana).
notes: nastaḥ pracchardana: expelling (doṣas) through the nose, i.e. errhine therapy. Count: 19 fruit-drugs minus 8 for emesis and āsthāpana (83b, 84a) minus 1 for nasal use (85a) = 10, as the text says.

hindi: उन्नीस फल नाम और कर्म से बताए गए। घी, तेल, वसा और मज्जा — स्नेह चार प्रकार का बताया गया है,
english: The nineteen fruits have been described by name and action. Ghee, oil, muscle fat and marrow: fat (sneha) is taught as fourfold,
notes: ekonaviṃśati = eka-ūna-viṃśati "twenty less one" = nineteen. vasā = fat of muscle tissue; majjā = bone marrow (in Sanskrit majjan/majjā; gender varies).

hindi: जो पान, अभ्यङ्ग, बस्ति और नस्य के लिए प्रयोग के अनुसार काम आता है। ये स्नेहन करने वाले, जीवन देने वाले, वर्ण के लिए हितकर तथा बल और शरीर की पुष्टि बढ़ाने वाले हैं।
english: for drinking, massage, enema and nasal medication, according to application. They are oleating, vitalising, good for the complexion, and increase strength and bodily bulk.
notes: yogataḥ may mean "according to the (proper) application" or "in combination (with other drugs)".

hindi: ये स्नेह वात, पित्त और कफ को दूर करने वाले बताए गए हैं। सौवर्चल, सैन्धव, विड और औद्भिद भी,
english: These fats are prescribed as removers of Vāta, Pitta and Kapha. Sauvarcala, saindhava (rock salt), viḍa and audbhida as well,
notes: The salt list continues into 89a. Identifications: saindhava = rock salt, Hindi सेंधा नमक (standard); sauvarcala = black salt, Hindi काला नमक or सौंचल (standard); viḍa = a manufactured salt, Hindi बिड़ नमक (standard); audbhida = salt that rises from the soil, efflorescent earth salt (probable).

hindi: ये समुद्री लवण के साथ पाँच लवण हैं। ये स्निग्ध, उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण और अग्नि को सबसे अधिक दीप्त करने वाले हैं।
english: together with sea salt (sāmudra), these are the five salts. They are unctuous, hot, sharp and the most kindling of the digestive fire.

text_flags.why: transposed aspirate: the word is snigdha "unctuous" (as in 100a snigdhaṃ, 107a snigdhaṃ).

hindi: ये लेप के लिए, स्नेहन और स्वेदन की विधि में, अधोभाग और ऊर्ध्वभाग शोधन में, निरूह में और अनुवासन में प्रयोग किए जाते हैं;
english: They are used for plasters, likewise in the procedures of oleation and sudation, in downward and upward evacuation, in decoction enemas (nirūha) and in unctuous enema (anuvāsana),
notes: adhobhāga and ūrdhvabhāga: evacuation downward (purgation) and upward (emesis). The list of uses continues in 91–92.

hindi: अभ्यङ्ग में, भोजन के लिए, सिर के विरेचन में, शस्त्रकर्म में, वर्ति के लिए, तथा अञ्जन और उत्सादन में;
english: in massage, for food, in evacuation of the head, in surgical operations, for suppositories (varti), and in collyria and unctions,

text_flags.why: cirecana is not a word; śirasaḥ virecana "evacuation of the head" is the parallel of śīrṣavirecane in 79b; c/v confusion.

notes: utsādana: rubbing the body with a paste or powder.

hindi: और अजीर्ण, आनाह, वात रोग, गुल्म, शूल तथा उदर रोग में। लवण बता दिए गए; अब आगे मुझसे आठ मूत्रों को जानो,
english: and in indigestion and distension (ānāha), in Vāta disorder, in gulma (abdominal lump), colic and udara (abdominal enlargement). The salts have been described; next learn from me the eight urines,
notes: vāte: "in (disorders of) Vāta"; it could also be taken narrowly as flatulence. ānāha = distension with retention of faeces and wind.

hindi: जो प्रमुख हैं और सब आत्रेय के उपदेश में बताए गए हैं: भेड़ का मूत्र, बकरी का मूत्र, गाय का मूत्र और जो भैंस का है,
english: the principal ones, all of which are taught in the teaching of Ātreya: sheep urine, goat urine, cow urine, and that of the buffalo,
notes: mukhyāni continues the object of nibodha in 92b (acc.); yāni ... diṣṭāni is a relative clause.

hindi: हाथी का मूत्र, तथा ऊँट, घोड़े और गधे का मूत्र। मूत्र उष्ण, तीक्ष्ण, अरूक्ष, कटु और लवण रस से युक्त होता है।
english: elephant urine, and that of the camel, the horse and the donkey. (Urine is) hot, sharp, not dry, pungent and accompanied by salt taste.
notes: atho'rūkṣam as printed with avagraha = atho arūkṣam "and not dry". Without the avagraha it would read atho rūkṣam "and dry"; the two readings give opposite properties, and editions and commentators differ. Kept as printed. The subject of line b (mūtram, urine in general) is understood.

hindi: मूत्र उत्सादन में प्रयुक्त होता है, लेपों में प्रयुक्त होता है, आस्थापन में प्रयुक्त होता है और विरेचन में भी प्रयुक्त होता है;
english: Urine is used in unction, used in plasters, used in decoction enema (āsthāpana), and used also in purgation,
notes: yuktam can mean "used" or "suitable"; rendered "used".

hindi: स्वेदों में भी वह प्रयुक्त होता है, तथा आनाह में, अगदों में, उदर रोगों में, अर्श में, और गुल्म, कुष्ठ तथा किलास के रोगियों में;
english: it is used also in sudations, in distension and in antidotes, in abdominal enlargements (udara) and in piles, and for those suffering from gulma, skin disease (kuṣṭha) and kilāsa (white patches of skin, leucoderma);
notes: kilāsa: a white skin disease, usually equated with leucoderma or vitiligo (probable). kuṣṭha covers skin diseases broadly, including but not limited to leprosy. ānāha in the context of a list of procedures could also mean a kind of sudation, but the plain sense "distension" is kept.

hindi: वह उपनाहों में और परिषेक में भी प्रयुक्त होता है। उसे अग्निदीपक, विषनाशक और कृमिनाशक बताया जाता है।
english: it is used in poultices (upanāha) and likewise in affusion (pariṣeka). It is taught to be kindling of the digestive fire, destroying poison and destroying worms.
notes: pariṣeka: pouring liquid over the body or a part.

words.gram: tat-puruṣa, ppp. m. gen. pl. upa-√sṛj

words.gloss: would move in the right direction

hindi: पाण्डुरोग से पीड़ित लोगों के लिए इसे उत्तम सुख देने वाला कहा गया है। पिया हुआ मूत्र कफ को शान्त करता है और वायु का अनुलोमन करता है,
english: and it is said to be the best relief for those afflicted with pāṇḍu disease (pallor, anaemia). When drunk it pacifies Kapha (śleṣman) and moves wind (māruta, Vāta) in its proper direction,

text_flags.why: ppp. of upa-√sṛj is upasṛṣṭa with retroflex ṭ; dental t is a typing slip.

notes: pāṇḍu roga: a disease of pallor, usually equated with anaemia (standard). anulomayet: makes Vāta move downward, in its natural direction.

hindi: और पित्त को नीचे के मार्ग से निकालता है। इस प्रकार इसका गुण-संग्रह मैंने सामान्य रूप से कहा; अब अलग-अलग कहा जाएगा।
english: and draws Pitta out downwards. Thus the summary of its properties has been told by me in general terms; it will now be described separately.
notes: asmin: "in this (urine)". pravakṣyate is formally a future middle, used here in a passive sense.

hindi: भेड़ का मूत्र तिक्त रस से युक्त, स्निग्ध और पित्त का विरोधी न होने वाला है। बकरी का मूत्र कषाय और मधुर, पथ्य है और दोषों को नष्ट करता है।
english: Sheep urine is slightly bitter, unctuous and not hostile to Pitta. Goat urine is astringent and sweet, wholesome, and destroys the doṣas.
notes: satikta: "with bitterness", i.e. having a bitter taste in addition (often rendered "slightly bitter"). pittāvirodhi: literally "not hostile to Pitta", i.e. does not provoke it.
lines_deva: अविमूत्रं सतिक्तं स्यात् स्निग्धं पित्ताविरोधि च
lines_iast: avimūtraṃ satiktaṃ syāt snigdhaṃ pittāvirodhi ca

hindi: गाय का मूत्र कुछ मधुर, कुछ दोषनाशक, कृमि और कुष्ठ को दूर करने वाला है। पिया हुआ यह खुजली को शान्त करता है और दोषज उदर रोग में भली-भाँति हितकर है।
english: Cow urine has some sweetness, is somewhat doṣa-destroying, and dispels worms and skin disease (kuṣṭha). When drunk it relieves itching and is properly beneficial in udara (abdominal enlargement) caused by the doṣas.
notes: kiṃcit may qualify samadhuram ("slightly sweet") or doṣaghnam ("somewhat doṣa-destroying"); both readings are possible. samyak may go with pītam ("when properly drunk") or with hitam. doṣodara is taken as udara arising from the doṣas.
lines_deva: कण्डूं च शमयेत् पीतं सम्यग्दोषोदरे हितम्
lines_iast: kaṇḍūṃ ca śamayet pītaṃ samyagdoṣodare hitam

words.gram: possessive -in on dvandva krimi-kuṣṭha, m. gen. pl.

hindi: भैंस का मूत्र अर्श, शोथ और उदर रोग को नष्ट करने वाला, क्षार से युक्त और सर है। हाथी का मूत्र लवण है और कृमि तथा कुष्ठ के रोगियों के लिए हितकर है।
english: Buffalo urine destroys piles, swelling (śopha) and udara, is alkaline and laxative (sara). Elephant urine is salty and beneficial for those suffering from worms and skin disease.
notes: krimi-kuṣṭhinām: "for those having worms and kuṣṭha" (krimi- as first member with kuṣṭhin).
lines_deva: हास्तिकं लवणं मूत्रं हितं तु क्रिमिकुष्ठिनाम्
lines_iast: hāstikaṃ lavaṇaṃ mūtraṃ hitaṃ tu krimikuṣṭhinām

hindi: वह मल-मूत्र के रुकने, विष, कफ के रोगों और अर्श में प्रशस्त है। ऊँट का मूत्र तिक्त रस से युक्त, श्वास, कास और अर्श को नष्ट करने वाला कहा जाता है।
english: It (elephant urine) is recommended for obstruction of faeces and urine, poison, Kapha disorders and piles. Camel urine is said to be slightly bitter and to destroy dyspnoea (śvāsa), cough and piles.
notes: Line a most naturally continues the elephant urine of 102b. The compound is read as baddha-viṇmūtra (retention of faeces and urine), viṣa, śleṣmāmaya (Kapha disorders), arśas; other groupings are possible. śvāsa: difficult breathing, often equated with asthma (probable).

hindi: घोड़ों का मूत्र तिक्त और कटु है तथा कुष्ठ, व्रण और विष को दूर करता है। गधे का मूत्र अपस्मार, उन्माद और ग्रह-बाधा को नष्ट करने वाला है।
english: That of horses is bitter and pungent and removes skin disease, wounds and poison. Donkey urine destroys epilepsy (apasmāra), insanity (unmāda) and seizure by spirits (graha).
notes: vājinām: genitive plural, with mūtram understood. apasmāra = epilepsy (standard); unmāda = insanity, psychosis (standard); graha = possession or seizure by supernatural beings, as the text conceives it.

hindi: इस प्रकार यहाँ मूत्र उनके सामर्थ्य और प्रयोग के अनुसार बताए गए। अब दूध बताए जाएँगे, और इनका कर्म तथा जो इनके गुण हैं।
english: Thus the urines have been described here according to their efficacy and application. Next the milks will be described, with their action and their properties.
notes: yathāsāmarthyayogataḥ could also mean "according to their efficacy in combination (with other drugs)".
lines_deva: अतः क्षीराणि वक्ष्यन्ते कर्म चैषां गुणाश्च ये
lines_iast: ataḥ kṣīrāṇi vakṣyante karma caiṣāṃ guṇāśca ye

hindi: भेड़ का दूध, बकरी का दूध, गाय का दूध और जो भैंस का है, फिर ऊँटनियों का, हथिनियों का, घोड़ी का और स्त्री का दूध।
english: Sheep milk, goat milk, cow milk and that of the buffalo; then that of she-camels, of she-elephants, of the mare and likewise of woman.
notes: Eight milks, as stated in 75b.

hindi: दूध प्रायः मधुर, स्निग्ध, शीत और स्तन्य बढ़ाने वाला माना गया है; यह तृप्त करने वाला, बृंहण, वृष्य, मेधा के लिए हितकर, बलकारक और मन को स्फूर्ति देने वाला है,
english: Milk is generally held to be sweet, unctuous, cold and promoting of breast milk; it is nourishing, bulk-promoting (bṛṃhaṇa), aphrodisiac, good for the intellect, strengthening and invigorating to the mind,
notes: stanyam: taken as "promoting breast milk" (galactagogue); it could also be read as "(like) breast milk". manaskara: literally "mind-making", i.e. invigorating or cheering the mind.
lines_deva: प्रायशो मधुरं स्निग्धं शीतं स्तन्यं पयो मतम्
प्रीणनं बृंहणं वृष्यं मेध्यं बल्यं मनस्करम्
lines_iast: prāyaśo madhuraṃ snigdhaṃ śītaṃ stanyaṃ payo matam
prīṇanaṃ bṛṃhaṇaṃ vṛṣyaṃ medhyaṃ balyaṃ manaskaram

hindi: जीवनीय, थकान दूर करने वाला, श्वास और कास को मिटाने वाला है; यह रक्तपित्त को नष्ट करता है और आहत को जोड़ने वाला है,
english: vitalising, removing fatigue, removing dyspnoea and cough; it destroys śoṇitapitta (bleeding disorder) and is a uniter of what is injured,
notes: śoṇitapitta = raktapitta, a bleeding disorder (haemorrhage from various orifices) (standard). vihatasya: of an injured or broken (part); sandhāna = joining, healing. The sentence continues into the next unit.
lines_deva: हन्ति शोणितपित्तं च सन्धानं विहतस्य च
lines_iast: hanti śoṇitapittaṃ ca sandhānaṃ vihatasya ca

words.gloss: in the wasted and the injured

hindi: दूध सभी प्राणियों के लिए सात्म्य है, शमन करने वाला और शोधन करने वाला भी है, प्यास बुझाने वाला और अग्नि को दीप्त करने वाला है, तथा क्षीण और क्षत रोगियों के लिए श्रेष्ठ है।
english: (Milk) is wholesome (sātmya) for all living beings, both pacifying (śamana) and purifying (śodhana), thirst-quenching and appetising (dīpanīya), and the best thing for the wasted and the injured (kṣīṇa-kṣata).

text_flags.why: possible typo: the compound is prāṇa-bhṛt 'bearer of breath'; a long ā before bhṛ has no grammatical basis; syllable count is the same either way

notes: Subject 'milk' (payaḥ/kṣīra) is carried over from the preceding verses. kṣīṇa-kṣata may mean 'those wasted and those with (chest) injury' or a single class 'wasted from chest injury (urakṣata)'; taken here as dvandva.
lines_deva: तृष्णाघ्नं दीपनीयं च श्रेष्ठं क्षीणक्षतेषु च
lines_iast: tṛṣṇāghnaṃ dīpanīyaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ kṣīṇakṣateṣu ca

hindi: यह विशेष रूप से पाण्डुरोग, अम्लपित्त, शोष, गुल्म और उदररोग में, तथा अतिसार, ज्वर, दाह और शोथ में हितकर है।
english: It is especially (beneficial) in anaemia (pāṇḍu-roga), acid dyspepsia (amlapitta), wasting (śoṣa), abdominal lump (gulma) and abdominal enlargement (udara), and in diarrhoea (atīsāra), fever, burning sensation and swelling (śvayathu).
notes: The verb ('is beneficial') is implied from the context of 109. Modern equivalents are the usual approximations: pāṇḍu = anaemia; amlapitta = hyperacidity; śoṣa = consumption/wasting; gulma = abdominal lump or tumour; udara = abdominal enlargement including ascites.
lines_deva: अतीसारे ज्वरे दाहे श्वयथौ च विशेषतः
lines_iast: atīsāre jvare dāhe śvayathau ca viśeṣataḥ

words.gloss: in disorders of vagina and semen

hindi: योनि और शुक्र के दोषों में, अल्प मूत्र में और गाँठदार कठोर मल में यह हितकर है, तथा वात और पित्त के विकारों से पीड़ित लोगों के लिए पथ्य है।
english: In disorders of the female genital tract (yoni) and of semen (śukra), in scanty urine, and in hard, knotted faeces, it is wholesome for those suffering from Vāta and Pitta disorders.
notes: yoni here may be the female reproductive organ generally; pradoṣa = disorder/vitiation.

words.gloss: in nasal therapy, plasters and baths

hindi: नस्य, लेप, अवगाहन, वमन, आस्थापन, विरेचन और स्नेहन में, सब जगह दूध का प्रयोग होता है।
english: In nasal therapy (nasya), plasters, immersion baths, emesis (vamana), decoction enemas (āsthāpana), purgation (virecana) and oleation (snehana): milk is used everywhere.
lines_deva: विरेचने स्नेहने च पयः सर्वत्र युज्यते
lines_iast: virecane snehane ca payaḥ sarvatra yujyate

hindi: हर एक के दूध के गुणों को अलग-अलग क्रम से मैं अन्नपान आदि वाले अध्याय में फिर पूरी तरह कहूँगा।
english: The properties of the milk of each (animal), one by one and in due order, I shall describe again in full in the chapter beginning with 'annapāna' (food and drink).
notes: ekaikasya 'of each' refers to the milk-giving animals listed earlier. The chapter meant is probably Sūtrasthāna 27 (Annapānavidhi); that is an inference, the text gives only the title phrase.

words.gloss: from the fruit- and root-yielding plants

hindi: अब तीन अन्य वृक्ष हैं, जो फलिनी और मूलिनी द्रव्यों से अलग हैं: स्नुही, अर्क और अश्मन्तक। उनका कर्म अलग-अलग इस प्रकार है।
english: Now there are three other trees, separate from the fruit- and root-yielding plants: snuhī, arka and aśmantaka. Their action, one by one, is as follows.
notes: Identifications: snuhī = Euphorbia neriifolia, Hindi थूहर/सेहुंड (standard); arka = Calotropis procera or C. gigantea, Hindi आक/मदार (standard); aśmantaka = disputed (Bauhinia racemosa and Ficus species have been proposed).

hindi: वमन में अश्मन्तक को जानना चाहिए, विरेचन में स्नुही के दूध को; और अर्क का दूध विरेचन सहित वमन में जानना चाहिए।
english: One should know aśmantaka (as used) for emesis and the latex of snuhī for purgation; the latex of arka is to be known (as used) for emesis together with purgation.
notes: kṣīra here means the plant latex, not milk. 'vamane savirecane' read as 'in emesis accompanied by purgation', i.e. arka latex acts both ways.

hindi: इन तीन अन्य वृक्षों को बताते हैं जिनकी छालें हितकर हैं: पूतीक, कृष्णगन्धा और तिल्वक वृक्ष।
english: They name these three other trees whose barks are beneficial: pūtīka, kṛṣṇagandhā and likewise the tree tilvaka.
notes: Identifications: pūtīka = disputed (Holoptelea integrifolia and pūtikarañja, Caesalpinia bonduc, are both proposed); kṛṣṇagandhā = probable Moringa oleifera, drumstick, Hindi सहजन (identified with śigru by commentators); tilvaka = disputed (Symplocos racemosa, lodhra, and Viburnum species proposed).
lines_deva: पूतीकः कृष्णगन्धा च तिल्वकश्च तथा तरुः
lines_iast: pūtīkaḥ kṛṣṇagandhā ca tilvakaśca tathā taruḥ

hindi: विरेचन में पूतीक और तिल्वक का प्रयोग करना चाहिए; कृष्णगन्धा परीसर्प, शोथ और अर्श में बताई गई है।
english: Pūtīka and likewise tilvaka are to be used for purgation; kṛṣṇagandhā is prescribed in spreading skin disease (parīsarpa), in swellings and in piles (arśas),

text_flags.why: possible spelling error: loc. pl. of arśas is arśaḥsu (no retroflex ṣ after a-visarga); sense and metre unaffected

notes: The list of diseases for kṛṣṇagandhā continues into unit 118 (sentence continuation, grouping is correct). parīsarpa = visarpa, usually equated with erysipelas (approximate).

words.gloss: in ringworm, abscess and glandular swellings

hindi: दद्रु, विद्रधि, गण्ड, कुष्ठ और अलजी में भी; और विवेकशील व्यक्ति इन छह वृक्षों को शोधन करने वाला भी जाने।
english: and in ringworm (dadru), abscess (vidradhi), glandular swellings (gaṇḍa), skin diseases (kuṣṭha) and alajī eruptions. The discerning (physician) should also know these six trees as purifying (śodhana).
notes: Line a continues the diseases for kṛṣṇagandhā from unit 117. gaṇḍa may mean goitre or glandular swelling; kuṣṭha covers skin diseases broadly, not only leprosy; alajī is a kind of boil or eruption (exact sense varies between texts).

words.gloss: whose latex and bark were indicated

hindi: इस प्रकार फलिनी और मूलिनी द्रव्य, स्नेह, लवण, मूत्र, दूध और वे छह वृक्ष जिनके दूध और छाल बताए गए हैं, कह दिए गए।
english: Thus have been stated the fruit- and root-yielding plants, the unctuous substances (sneha), the salts, urine, the milks, and the six trees whose latex and bark were indicated.
notes: diṣṭa-payas-tvacaḥ: three trees are used for their latex (payas) and three for their bark (tvak).
lines_deva: मूत्रं क्षीराणि वृक्षाश्च षड् ये दिष्टपयस्त्वचः
lines_iast: mūtraṃ kṣīrāṇi vṛkṣāśca ṣaḍ ye diṣṭapayastvacaḥ

hindi: वन में बकरी चराने वाले, भेड़ चराने वाले, गोपालक और जो अन्य वनवासी हैं, वे ओषधियों को नाम और रूप से जानते हैं।
english: Goatherds, shepherds, cowherds and the other forest-dwellers know the plants in the forest by their names and forms.
notes: vane may go with jānate ('know in the forest') or with the herdsmen ('herdsmen in the forest'); the sense is the same.

hindi: केवल नाम के ज्ञान से, या फिर रूप के ज्ञान से, कोई भी ओषधियों की परम प्राप्ति को नहीं जान सकता।
english: No one can know the highest mastery of plants by mere knowledge of their names, or again by knowledge of their forms.
notes: parāṃ prāptim 'highest attainment' is taken as full mastery of the plants (their right use); it could also be read as 'the highest benefit obtained from plants'.

hindi: परन्तु जो उनके प्रयोग को जानता है, वह रूप को न जानते हुए भी उनका तत्त्व जानने वाला कहलाता है; फिर उस वैद्य का तो कहना ही क्या जो ओषधियों को सब प्रकार से जानता हो।
english: But one who knows their application (yoga), even without knowing their form, is called a knower of their true nature; how much more, then, the physician who knows the plants in every respect!

hindi: जो वैद्य प्रत्येक व्यक्ति की परीक्षा करके देश और काल के अनुसार इनके प्रयोग को जानता है, उसे उत्तम वैद्य जानना चाहिए।
english: He who knows their application, adapted to place and time, after examining each person individually, is to be known as the best of physicians.
notes: puruṣaṃ puruṣam (repetition) = each individual person.
lines_deva: पुरुषं पुरुषं वीक्ष्य स ज्ञेयो भिषगुत्तमः
lines_iast: puruṣaṃ puruṣaṃ vīkṣya sa jñeyo bhiṣaguttamaḥ

hindi: जैसे विष, जैसे शस्त्र, जैसे अग्नि, जैसे वज्र होता है, वैसी ही बिना जानी हुई औषध होती है; और जानी हुई औषध अमृत के समान होती है।
english: Like poison, like a weapon, like fire, like a thunderbolt is a medicine that is not understood; a medicine well understood is like nectar (amṛta).

hindi: क्योंकि जो औषध नाम, रूप और गुण इन तीनों से न पहचानी गई हो, और जो जानी हुई होकर भी गलत ढंग से प्रयुक्त हो, वह अनर्थ का कारण बनती है।
english: For a medicine not recognised by the three, name, form and properties, and even one that is known but wrongly applied, leads to harm.

hindi: उचित प्रयोग से तीक्ष्ण विष भी उत्तम औषध बन सकता है, और गलत ढंग से प्रयुक्त औषध भी तीक्ष्ण विष बन जाती है।
english: Through proper application even a potent poison may become an excellent medicine, and a medicine wrongly applied becomes a potent poison.
notes: tīkṣṇa in line a may qualify viṣam ('potent poison') as taken here; grammatically it could also go with bheṣajam.
lines_deva: भेषजं चापि दुर्युक्तं तीक्ष्णं संपद्यते विषम्
lines_iast: bheṣajaṃ cāpi duryuktaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ saṃpadyate viṣam

hindi: इसलिए जीवन और आरोग्य चाहने वाले बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति को युक्ति से रहित वैद्य द्वारा दी गई कोई भी औषध नहीं लेनी चाहिए।
english: Therefore a wise person who desires life and health should not accept any medicine administered by a physician who is devoid of rational planning (yukti).
notes: yukti = reasoned planning of treatment; yukti-bāhya lit. 'outside yukti'.

hindi: सिर पर गिरा हुआ इन्द्र का वज्र भी शायद कुछ शेष छोड़ दे, परन्तु अज्ञानी द्वारा बताई गई औषध रोगी को कुछ भी शेष नहीं छोड़ती।
english: Vāsava's (Indra's) thunderbolt falling on the head might still leave something remaining; but a medicine prescribed by an ignorant person would not leave the patient with anything remaining.
notes: saśeṣa 'with a remainder' = left with some life. ajña-mata lit. 'thought fit by an ignorant one'.

words.gram: m. dat. sg. pres. part. śrad-√dhā

hindi: जो अपने को बुद्धिमान मानने वाला व्यक्ति औषध को बिना जाने दुःखी, शय्या पर पड़े, श्रद्धा रखने वाले रोगी को दे देता है,
english: He who, thinking himself wise, gives a medicine without knowing it to a suffering, bed-ridden and trusting patient,
notes: The sentence continues into unit 130 (the yaḥ of this verse is picked up by tasya there); grouping is correct.

words.gloss: of one who has abandoned dharma

hindi: उस धर्म को त्याग देने वाले, पापी, मृत्यु रूप, दुर्बुद्धि व्यक्ति से बात करने मात्र से भी मनुष्य नरक में गिरने वाला हो जाता है।
english: with that man, who has abandoned dharma, sinful, death incarnate, evil-minded, a person would fall into hell even by conversing.
notes: Completes the sentence begun in unit 129.

hindi: साँप का विष पी लेना, या उबला हुआ पिघला ताँबा पी लेना, अथवा तीव्र आग में तपाए हुए लोहे के गोले निगल लेना अच्छा है,
english: Better to drink a serpent's venom or boiled (molten) copper, or even to swallow iron balls heated in fierce fire,
notes: Sentence continues into unit 132 ('but not ...'). The visarga of bhakṣitāḥ and of -santaptāḥ is dropped by sandhi before a voiced sound.

words.gloss: from one who has come for refuge

hindi: परन्तु विद्वानों का वेश धारण करने वाले व्यक्ति द्वारा शरण में आए हुए रोगपीड़ित से अन्न, पान या धन लेना अच्छा नहीं है।
english: but not (better) is food, drink or money taken, by one who wears the guise of the learned, from a disease-stricken person who has come to him for refuge.
notes: natu printed as one token = na tu. The predicate 'better' (varam) from unit 131 is understood: worse than those deadly acts is taking food, drink or wealth from a sick refugee while wearing the guise of the learned.
lines_deva: गृहीतमन्नं पानं वा वित्तं वा रोगपीडितात्
lines_iast: gṛhītamannaṃ pānaṃ vā vittaṃ vā rogapīḍitāt

hindi: इसलिए वैद्य बनने की इच्छा रखने वाला बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति अपने गुणों की सम्पदा प्राप्त करने में परम प्रयत्न करे, जिससे वह मनुष्यों का प्राणदाता हो सके।
english: Therefore an intelligent person wishing to become a physician should make the utmost effort to perfect his own qualities, so that he may be a giver of life to people.

hindi: वही औषध उचित है जो आरोग्य प्रदान करे, और वही वैद्यों में श्रेष्ठ है जो रोगों से मुक्त कर दे।
english: That alone is the proper medicine which brings about health, and he alone is the best of physicians who frees (people) from diseases.
lines_deva: स चैव भिषजां श्रेष्ठो रोगेभ्यो यः प्रमोचयेत्
lines_iast: sa caiva bhiṣajāṃ śreṣṭho rogebhyo yaḥ pramocayet

hindi: सिद्धि सब कर्मों के सही प्रयोग को बताती है, और सिद्धि सब गुणों से युक्त श्रेष्ठ वैद्य को बताती है।
english: Success reveals the correct application of all therapeutic actions; and success reveals the best physician, endowed with all qualities.
notes: karman here = therapeutic procedure (karma = action per glossary).

hindi: यहाँ ये श्लोक हैं: आयुर्वेद का आगमन, उसके आगमन का कारण, उसका प्रवर्तन, सूत्ररचना का अनुमोदन, आयुर्वेद का निर्णय,
english: Here are the verses: the coming of Āyurveda (the science of life), the reason for its coming, its propagation, the approval of the composition (of treatises), the definition of Āyurveda,
notes: 'tatra ślokāḥ' is the lead-in formula of the closing summary; it is kept as line a of this numbered verse as the edition groups it. The list (a catalogue of topics in nom.) runs on to unit 140.

hindi: पूर्ण कारण, कार्य, आयुर्वेद का प्रयोजन, रोगों के हेतु, दोष और संक्षेप में औषध,
english: the complete cause (kāraṇa), the effect (kārya), the purpose of Āyurveda, the causes (of disease), the doṣas and, in brief, medicine,
notes: saṃpūrṇaṃ kāraṇam probably refers to the six fundamental causes (sāmānya, viśeṣa, guṇa, dravya, karma, samavāya) treated in the chapter; this is an interpretation. saṃgraheṇa 'in brief' may qualify only bheṣajam or the whole list.

words.gloss: with the substances that are their source

hindi: रस, उनके आश्रय रूप द्रव्यों सहित, द्रव्यों का तीन प्रकार का संग्रह, मूलिनी और फलिनी द्रव्य, स्नेह और लवण,
english: the tastes (rasa) together with the substances that are their source, the threefold classification of substances, the root-yielding and fruit-yielding plants, the unctuous substances and the salts,
notes: sa-pratyaya-dravyāḥ is uncertain: 'with their causes, the substances' or 'with the substances that are their basis (pratyaya)'; the second is taken here.

words.gloss: merits and demerits of proper and improper use

hindi: मूत्र, दूध, और वे छह वृक्ष जिनका उपयोग दूध और छाल पर आधारित है, इन सबके कर्म, और उचित तथा अनुचित प्रयोग के गुण और दोष,
english: urine, the milks, the six trees whose use rests on latex and bark, the actions of all these, the merits of proper use and the faults of improper use,
notes: yoga-ayoga-guṇa-aguṇāḥ may also be read as four items: proper use, improper use, merits, demerits.
lines_deva: मूत्रं क्षीराणि वृक्षाश्च षड् ये क्षीरत्वगाश्रयाः
lines_iast: mūtraṃ kṣīrāṇi vṛkṣāśca ṣaḍ ye kṣīratvagāśrayāḥ

hindi: वैद्य की निन्दा, और जहाँ वैद्यों के सब गुण स्थित हैं, यह सब महर्षि ने पहले अध्याय में भली भाँति कहा है।
english: the censure of physicians, and (the passage) where all the qualities of physicians are found: all this has been explained by the great sage in the first chapter.
notes: yatrasthāḥ 'located where' is elliptical: the verses in which all the physician's qualities are stated. The great sage is not named here.
lines_deva: वैद्यापवादो यत्रस्थाः सर्वे च भिषजां गुणाः
lines_iast: vaidyāpavādo yatrasthāḥ sarve ca bhiṣajāṃ guṇāḥ

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित और चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के सूत्रस्थान में दीर्घञ्जीवितीय नामक पहला अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the Sūtrasthāna of the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, the first chapter, named Dīrghañjīvitīya (On long life).
notes: Chapter colophon. The title is taken from the chapter's opening words (dīrghaṃ jīvitam). The Sanskrit has no verb; the translation keeps it verbless.
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते सूत्रस्थाने दीर्घञ्जीवितीयो नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte sūtrasthāne dīrghañjīvitīyo nāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ
